items.title: Ads in Chatbots Have Arrived. Here’s What’s Working—and What’s Not
items.summary: As Anthropic maintains its vow to keep ads out of Claude, the rest of the AI chatbot industry is racing to win over advertisers without antagonizing users.
items.author: Paresh Dave

items.title: Reddit Founder Says Building Social Media Apps Is ‘Not Cool Anymore’
items.summary: Alexis Ohanian is trying to figure out what’s next for user-generated content now that so much of the internet is “compromised.”
items.author: Isabella Ward

items.title: Exclusive: Aina’s Smart Ring Wants to Be a Remote Control for Your AI Agent
items.summary: The startup Aina bets you won’t need to rely on your phone to control virtual assistants. It’s making a smart ring that lets you control the actions of your autonomous agents with one tap.
items.author: Julian Chokkattu

items.title: Finding New Drugs Is Laborious. This AI Startup Is Skipping The Lab Work
items.summary: Potential Sciences, a startup backed by the UK government, is betting that training AI models on computer-generated biochemical data can speed up the plodding process of developing new drugs.
items.author: Joel Khalili

items.title: AI’s Next Trick? Speaking Dolphin
items.summary: Denise Herzing, the founder and director of the Wild Dolphin Project, is using AI to help understand audio and video footage of the marine mammals.
items.author: Kate Taylor

items.title: He Trolls AI Labs for a Living. Now They All Want to Work With Him
items.summary: OpenAI, Anthropic, and SpaceXSI have all reached out to Husk, an influencer who regularly goes viral by exposing the shortcomings of chatbots.
items.author: Isabella Ward
